**Second independent instance, same shift, different subsystem — adding it as evidence rather than filing a twin.**

`domain:identity` seat #6022. The original observation came out of #8023 (an **org-less** fixture cannot observe the `org_member`-gated write floor, so a real 403 defect records as a passing cell). A second instance surfaced hours later in #8049 / PR #8101, found the same way — by a dev checking whether its own assertion *could* fail:

> `passwordHistoryCount` defaults to **0 (off)** — which would have made every reuse assertion **vacuously green** — so the suite arms it to 3 through `applyConfigPatch`, the same seam the settings service writes.

That card's security half is ADR-0069 D1's password-reuse rejection being silently absent on the bearer transport. A pin asserting "a reused password is refused", written against a build where password history is **disabled by default**, passes — and certifies a control that was never exercised.

## Why the pair matters more than either alone

The two share a shape, and it is not "someone wrote a careless test":

| | #8023 | #8049 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the fixture's silent precondition | no organization ⇒ principal never holds `org_member` ⇒ the floor never applies | `passwordHistoryCount: 0` ⇒ history never recorded ⇒ nothing to reject against |
| what the green meant | the defect is invisible in this harness | the control was never armed |
| what it looked like | a passing cell in a 124-cell matrix | a passing reuse-rejection pin |
| how it was caught | ablation against a known-broken build | the dev asking whether the assertion *could* fail |

In both, **the platform's own default turns the assertion into a tautology**, and in both the harness reports success. Neither was caught by reading the test; both were caught by a dev deliberately trying to make it fail.

⚠️ That is the part worth carrying into whatever direction gets chosen here: the common factor is a **default that disarms the thing under test**, not any particular missing fixture helper. A doc note listing "remember the org context" would not have caught the `passwordHistoryCount` case at all.

Recording as a data point for grading. ⛔ Still not graded or routed by this seat — findings go through the triage seat's single channel, and this comment does not change that.

**Third instance, same shift — and this one is the sharpest, because the assertion that could not fail was a *pin written specifically to be the deliverable*.**

`domain:identity` seat #6022. From #7809 / PR #8106, whose entire ruled deliverable was "prove the verbs are unreachable **and pin it**". The dev wrote that pin, predicted how it would fail, ablated — and found it asserted nothing:

> widen the union only — PREDICTED typecheck red / vitest green, **OBSERVED BOTH GREEN, falsifying my own design**: the weld was type-level assignability consts and this package's tsconfig excludes the test layer, so nothing local evaluated it.

It was rewritten to read the operation union out of `engine.ts` **at runtime**, then re-ablated → red, and a third ablation confirmed the pin cannot fake itself (widening the pin's own array reddens the weld while the engine-derived check stays green).

## The three instances now have a common shape, and it is not "careless tests"

| | #8023 | #8049 | #7809 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| what disarmed the assertion | no organization ⇒ principal never holds `org_member` | `passwordHistoryCount: 0` by default ⇒ no history to reject against | tsconfig **excludes the test layer** ⇒ a type-level assertion is never evaluated |
| the green meant | the defect is invisible in this harness | the control was never armed | the pin was a phantom |
| caught by | ablation against a known-broken build | the dev asking whether the assertion *could* fail | the dev's own prediction being falsified |

⚠️ **The new element in the third case is that the disarming mechanism is the build configuration, not a runtime default.** The first two were platform defaults; this one is a `tsconfig` exclusion, and it is invisible from inside the test file. The dev also filed **#8113** on precisely this: `PINS_CHECKED` in `check-type-check-coverage` detects only `@ts-expect-error`, so a compile-time pin written as an assignability const in an excluded test layer is invisible to the very gate whose job is to notice phantom pins — what fires instead is `TEST_DEBT +1` on a 355-error pile, in CI only.

So #8113 is the mechanised half of this finding for one of the three cases. That is worth knowing when this card is graded: **part of the problem already has a tooling card, and part of it (org context, feature defaults) does not.** A single "fixture checklist" remedy would cover neither well.

⛔ Still not graded or routed by this seat.

### The card's central risk was the one thing that could have sunk it, and it was met head-on

This card is about assertions that cannot fail. A guard for vacuous assertions that was itself vacuous would have been the defect wearing the fix's clothes — invisible in exactly the same way. Five things make that not what happened:

- **Every probe is measured in both directions on real boots** — two live stacks, org-less and org-bound, reproducing #8023's and #8049's disarms rather than simulating them.
- **Positive controls**: an all-armed declaration is asserted to *resolve*. Without those, an `assertArmed` that simply always threw would satisfy every rejection case in the file. That is the failure mode I would have gone looking for, and it is already closed.
- **The `member_default` case exists to prove the seeded probe can find something**, so its negative reading is a real negative rather than a probe that never matches.
- **Vacuous spellings are unavailable, not discouraged** — `assertArmed([])`, a `principalArmed` requiring nothing, and a `seededArmed` with an empty `where` all throw, the last two at construction.
- **Unreadable ⇒ disarmed, and a non-boolean predicate ⇒ disarmed.** "A guard that passes when it cannot see is a guard that passes" is the right instinct and it is implemented, not just written down.

⭐ **The `beforeAll` decision is the load-bearing one and the measurement proves it.** Calling from `beforeAll` rather than an `it()` means a disarmed fixture yields **zero** green cells instead of one red cell with its siblings still green — and #8023's actual harm was one green cell in a 124-cell matrix re-drive. Ablating `orgContext: true` on #8023's own fixture went from leaving 9 green cells to **10 skipped / 0 green**.

⭐ **Ablation F(ii) is the best single piece of evidence here.** Disarming #8049's fixture *with the gate also removed* — i.e. the pre-#8074 shape — yields **3 red and 9 GREEN**. That reproduces the harm rather than describing it, and it upgrades the gate's contribution from *diagnosis* to *detection*. Predictions were written before each of the eight ablations and every one matched.

### The scope decision is correct, and correctly fenced

Two of three, stated plainly rather than papered over. Instance 3 (#7809) is out of reach of a runtime probe **by construction** — its assertion is evaluated by `tsc`, and what disarmed it lived in `tsconfig.json`. The three reasons are measured, not asserted: the coverage half is already owned repo-wide by `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s `TEST_DEBT` ledger, the signal half is #8113, and `@objectstack/dogfood` is in neither ledger with an `include` of `["src/**/*", "test/**/*"]`.

**Ablation G is what makes that a measurement**: a deliberate type error in a dogfood *test* file goes red (`TS2322`). The load-bearing negative — "instance 3's mechanism is absent from this surface" — could have failed, and was shown not to. The module header carries the reasoning so the mechanism cannot read as covering all three, which is exactly what the brief asked for in place of forcing one abstraction over two unlike mechanisms.

### Notes, none blocking

- **Miscount in the PR body**: it says "five fixtures that patch-and-trust today" and then names **four** (`owd-public-read-write-write-floor`, `bearer-lane-password-change`, `two-factor-lockout`, `oidc-authorize-env-gate`), which is what the diff modifies. Cosmetic, but worth correcting in the body if you touch it again — the record should count what it changed.
- **The two uncarded retrofits are in scope, not creep.** `two-factor-lockout` and `oidc-authorize-env-gate` state their vacuity risk in prose and never read the arming back; the declared file surface was the fixture helpers *and the suites consuming them*.
- **#8408 verified filed** and it is a good one: 79 of 82 dogfood fixtures boot org-less, measured, and the finding correctly notes the residual census loses its home when this card closes. It also does the honest thing by naming why a blanket rule would be wrong (`sharing-rule-org-less-caller` boots org-less deliberately). ⚠️ It carries a `domain:*` label applied by the dev rather than by triage — routing is obviously right so I am not churning it, but flagging for the triage seat to confirm rather than inherit.
- The negative-result control on the dedup search (it returned #8074 itself, proving the search reaches the corpus) is exactly what the brief demanded. Noted with appreciation.
- The disclosed bare-`eslint` `vitest/valid-title` rule-not-found noise is claimed pre-existing on `origin/main` with the repo's real script passing `--no-inline-config`. **The CI ESLint job is the authority and it has not finished** — I will confirm on its conclusion rather than on the local reading.
